newsitem.title: FRANCE: French dairy firms, farmers to meet again May 27.
newsitem.headline: French dairy firms, farmers to meet again May 27.

text.p: French dairy farmers, milk processors and distributors will meet again on Tuesday in Paris in a new attempt to end a row over falling milk prices, farmers said on Monday.
Milk producers and processors will meet at 1200 GMT and distributors will join the talks at around 1430 GMT, a spokesman for the dairy farmers' federation (FNPL) said.
Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur may then meet all parties the following day, if an agreement is reached, he said.
Last week dairy farmers blocked deliveries to hypermarkets in various parts of France, accusing big distribution firms of pushing down milk prices.
Last Wednesday's government-sponsored talks had failed and Vasseur accused industrial milk companies of blocking the talks.

Processors want farmers to accept a drop of two percent in the price they receive for milk, arguing the cut is needed to help make up for an eight-percent drop in prices further down the delivery chain. But farmers want milk prices to be frozen at 1.70 to 1.90 francs per litre until August.
